title: HTTP API
description: Can design and implement HTTP APIs whose methods, status codes and error bodies match a written contract — and can evolve that contract without casually breaking consumers.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can capture and annotate a raw HTTP request and response, implement routes whose status codes match the outcome, and name which route is idempotent and which is not — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can ship a minimal HTTP API whose OpenAPI document agrees with the implementation, whose errors are a consistent JSON shape with no stack traces or secrets, and whose curl smoke test exercises every route including failure cases.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently add a resource that touches more than one store inside a transaction, return 4xx not 500 for invalid input, and keep OpenAPI request and response schemas in agreement with the running service.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a client failure where a 200-with-error-body, a non-idempotent GET, or a leaked stack would look like success, cite the captured request and the contract clause that forbids it, and produce a compatibility matrix plus deprecation path another team can follow without reading the server source.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's API or OpenAPI document, name a status code, method or leaked error detail that violates HTTP semantics, and teach when a change is compatible versus breaking on an unfamiliar contract.
